I1.quote: Hydrogen adsorption measurements of activated carbons were carried out in a Hiden IMI PSI brand hydrogen storage device at 77 K. Before analysis, the materials were degassed at 105°C for 4 hours.
I1.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 552), Section 2.3 Hydrogen storage analysis

I2.quote: The carbons were synthesized by chemical activation using ZnCl₂ and characterized by BET surface area and pore analysis.

I3.quote: measured as a function of pressure at 77 K up to 80 bar. Horse chestnut-based activated carbon showed higher performance with a maximum hydrogen adsorption capacity of 4.47% at 80 bar
I3.location: main, p. 1 (journal p. 550), Abstract; values also in Table 1, main p. 3

I4.quote: The BET surface area of the horse chestnut-based activated carbon was determined as 2128 m²/g, while this value was at the level of 1230 m²/g for the tangerine peel-based activated carbon.
I4.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 552), Section 3.1 and Table 1

I5.quote: In this study, the hydrogen storage capacities and adsorption behaviors of activated carbons obtained from agricultural wastes such as tangerine peel and horse chestnut were investigated in detail.
I5.location: main, p. 1 (journal p. 550), Abstract, first sentence

notes: Research article (header 'Research Article'); record is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF. Single main PDF, no SI files. Synthesis procedures cite refs [16] (tangerine peel AC, H2 storage, 2020) and [18] (horse chestnut shell AC, H2 storage, 2024) by overlapping authors, and the Introduction says those studies reported storage capacity; but the paper does not state that its own uptake values were published before, and Table 2 labels them 'In this study', so duplicate_data is not applied. The paper names the instrument but not the method class (volumetric/gravimetric) in words. For extraction: Table 4 qe(exp) at 80 bar for horse chestnut shell is 3.336 mmol/g (about 0.67 wt%), which does not match the 4.47 wt% at 80 bar in Table 1.
